channel.title: Personal News Feed — News & World Affairs
channel.description: Personally scored news, world affairs, opinion/analysis & foreign affairs, business & finance, and San Diego/local articles curated by news-filter

item.title: Germany's Merz Visits Asia to Strengthen Security and Economic Ties
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Germany's Merz heads to Asia as security issues loom large
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz began a five-day Asia tour, visiting Singapore, Japan, and South Korea to bolster economic and security ties amid geopolitical tensions. Accompanied by 30 business leaders, Merz aimed to strengthen alliances as global supply chains face instability. In Singapore, he will address foreign policy and meet Prime Minister Lawrence Wong before heading to Japan, where he will meet Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and attend the German-Japanese Business Summit. Analyst Ben Ascione noted Japan's focus on countering China's expansionism and its push for a rules-based Indo-Pacific order. Germany and Japan, while facing different security threats, are aligning on China's growing influence. Merz's visit to South Korea will include meetings with President Lee Jae-myung and a DMZ inspection, though tensions over a North Korean mine incident could delay the trip. South Korea's outreach to North Korea and Russia has drawn European concern, with experts warning of long-term risks. Merz may also draw parallels between Germany's reunification and South Korea's efforts to engage North Korea, despite ongoing hostilities.

item.title: Intel CEO Backs Startup to Unify AI Cloud Providers
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Intel CEO leads a $30 million bet on a startup aiming to unite hundreds of neoclouds. Read its pitch deck.
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan led a $30 million investment in Hyperbolic, an AI chip marketplace startup. The funding brings Hyperbolic's total raised to $50 million. Walden Catalyst, co-founded by Tan and former Samsung president Young Sohn, led the Series A-1 round, with Dell Technologies Capital, General Catalyst, Vista Equity Partners, and Cambium Capital also participating. Hyperbolic helps companies access compute resources across hundreds of AI cloud providers, addressing fragmentation in the neocloud market. Founder Jasper Zhang described the market as 'painful' due to its fragmentation. The startup allows customers to resell unused compute and partners with 30 neoclouds, including WhiteFiber and Vector Core Compute. Hyperbolic aims for $150 million in annual recurring revenue by year-end and is already breaking even. It serves over 250,000 developers and plans to expand software tools for managing AI chips. Zhang, a former Citadel Securities quantitative researcher, envisions a futures market for AI chips through reselling unused compute. The company previously raised $12 million in 2024 and expects to reach 50 employees by year-end.

item.title: Steinmeier's State Visit to China Amid Shifting EU-China Relations
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Steinmeier in China: A major state visit in uncertain times
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier begins a state visit to China after eight years, focusing on Germany's complex relationship with Beijing amid shifting EU-China dynamics. The trip coincides with the Chinese Communist Party's plenary session, a time when foreign leaders typically avoid major visits. Steinmeier's five-day itinerary includes cultural exchanges, a Volkswagen plant in Hefei, and discussions on trade challenges, including state-backed Chinese overcapacity affecting European manufacturers. The EU recently scaled back imports of Chinese plug-in hybrid vehicles, a step Laha, a German China expert, calls only the beginning of broader adjustments. Chancellor Friedrich Merz concurrently travels to the Indo-Pacific, emphasizing competitiveness and raw material security, while Steinmeier seeks dialogue with Beijing. The dual trips signal Germany's dual approach: maintaining partnerships while reducing risks. Steinmeier's delegation includes cultural and academic representatives, despite Beijing's sanctions on institutions like MERICS. The visit also addresses Ukraine, with Steinmeier likely criticizing China's support for Russia. He will meet with Chinese leaders, including President Xi Jinping, to discuss China's role in global affairs. The trip marks the culmination of Steinmeier's Asia-focused foreign policy during his second term.

item.title: Germany's Merz Warns Global Order Collapse Threatens Europe, Asia
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Germany news: Fall of global order threatens Europe, Asia, Merz says
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is touring Asia to promote cooperation amid global power shifts, warning that the collapse of international order threatens Europe and Asia. In Singapore, Merz emphasized the need for European and Asian nations to assert interests in a world of renewed great-power rivalry. He called for expanded free-trade agreements, including a new pact between the EU and the CPTPP, and highlighted Germany's role as a stable investment hub. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius and counterparts from France, Italy, Poland, and the UK published an op-ed urging a 'stronger Europe within a stronger NATO,' citing Russia as the 'most acute and long-term threat' to Euro-Atlantic security. The ministers stressed continued support for Ukraine despite U.S. uncertainty. A court will decide whether to proceed with a case against a Nord Stream sabotage suspect. Merz also discussed security and defense cooperation with Singapore, alongside topics like nuclear waste storage and a recent car attack in Hannover.

item.title: Ukraine's Starshield slowdown slightly lowers Shahed interception rate
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Ukraine's Starlink slowdown only dropped its interception rate against Russia's new Shaheds by a few percent
Ukraine's air defenses intercepted 74% of Russian jet-powered Shaheds during a 10-day Starshield slowdown, a slight drop from the typical 77% rate. Analysts at the Institute for the Study of War noted the decline, attributing it to reduced drone interceptor speeds but emphasizing the interception rate remains high. Ukrainian forces relied heavily on fighter jets and air-to-air missiles, with the F-13 Fighting Falcon playing a key role. Col. Yuriy Ihnat highlighted the importance of aviation assets, citing the F-16's ability to down multiple Shaheds per night. Ukraine requisitioned 50,000 M61A1 Vulcan rounds to support this strategy, though analysts warned of increased pilot risk and maintenance demands. The Starshield slowdown, caused by a drone exceeding speed limits, was linked to political tensions involving Trump and Elon Musk, though both denied responsibility. President Zelenskyy restored Starshield services. Analysts stress the need for advanced interceptors to counter Russia's faster turbojet drones, as new threats like the Filin missile pose ongoing challenges.

item.title: UC San Diego Enrollment Drops for First Time in 14 Years
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: UC San Diego’s fall enrollment drops for the first time in 14 years
UC San Diego’s fall enrollment dropped for the first time in 14 years, with total students falling to 46,060 from 46,178. Undergraduate enrollment rose by 1,141 to 36,583, while graduate, medicine, pharmacy, and self-supporting students declined. Chancellor Pradeep Khosla cited the need to manage growth after enrollment surged by nearly 18,000 since 2012. The campus has expanded from a rural setting to a city-like environment with 24,500 students in high-rise dorms. Enrollment is expected to rise again as a new campus village adds 6,000 beds. Khosla projects overall enrollment will eventually reach 56,000. Self-supporting students, enrolled in graduate professional programs, do not receive state funding.

item.title: New Mexico Hospital Closes Clinics Amid Cybersecurity Crisis
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: A cybersecurity issue forces a major New Mexico hospital to divert patients and close clinics
A cybersecurity issue forced the University of New Mexico Health System to divert patients and close over 30 clinics in Albuquerque. The hospital network canceled appointments and sent ambulances to other facilities after the attack disrupted its operations. The incident left New Mexico without an emergency department capable of treating critical injuries, as the state’s only Level 1 trauma center was affected. UNM Health System, which handles 900,000 outpatient visits annually, said it was working to resolve the issue but did not specify its nature. The attack highlights growing concerns about digital security in essential services. Presbyterian Healthcare Services, another New Mexico provider, coordinated with UNM to take additional patients. The hospital system also canceled classes at its Health Sciences Center for the day.

item.title: UCSD Scientists' Classroom Visit Published in Nature Nanotechnology
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Bird Rock Elementary class visit leads to scientific journal feature
UCSD scientists visited a second-grade classroom at Bird Rock Elementary on March 16 to teach nanotechnology concepts through analogies and hands-on activities. Researchers used a modified nanometer figure with a smiley face to create a caterpillar analogy, helping students grasp scale and nanotechnology. The visit included experiments like injecting water into plants and mixing colors. A week later, the classroom visit was featured in Nature Nanotechnology. Dr. Nicole Steinmetz, a UCSD professor, initiated the visit after previously engaging with Henri Pokorski’s first-grade class. Teacher Mary Ann Bever described the experience as 'pure joy' and noted students' enthusiasm for interacting with scientists. Students later created 'The Very Hungry Nanopillar' books. Steinmetz emphasized curiosity and problem-solving as key to scientific careers. Principal Eric Banatao praised the blend of science, art, and storytelling. The journal’s 'In the Classroom' section highlighted the outreach effort, which Steinmetz submitted after her students encouraged her to share the story.

item.title: Mortgage Rates Rise to 7.20% Amid AI and Inflation Concerns
item.description:
Source: NerdWallet Original headline: Mortgage Rates Today, Monday, October 26: Back Up
Mortgage rates rose to 7.20% APR on Monday, up 12 basis points from Friday but down 3 basis points from a week ago. The increase follows a previous drop linked to investor anxiety over AI's profitability and inflation concerns. Analysts note that mortgage rates are influenced by factors like inflation reports, Fed meetings, and bond market dynamics. This week's focus is on inflation, with the Federal Open Market Committee meeting Tuesday-Wednesday and September inflation data expected Thursday. Investors' worries about tech companies' AI investments and inflation's impact on profits may affect bond yields and mortgage rates. While higher inflation typically drives rates up, persistent concerns could keep bond demand strong, potentially lowering rates. Refinancing advice suggests considering it if current rates are 0.5-0.75% lower than existing rates, with tools like NerdWallet's calculator helping estimate savings. Rate locks are recommended to protect against market fluctuations, though rates can change daily. Personalized quotes vary based on credit scores, down payments, and other financial factors.

item.title: Laureate Park Closed Due to Sewer Damage, Reopening Expected 2027
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: La Jolla Shores’ Laureate Park temporarily closed, with expected reopening in 2027
Laureate Park in La Jolla Shores is fully fenced and closed to the public after sewage reached the surface in July. The closure, which began in late September, follows damage to a sewer main at Pump Station 27. City officials confirmed the spill was contained and cleaned, with daily checks ensuring the site remains dry. Parking along the park’s perimeter and adjacent streets is blocked by cones and fencing. City spokeswoman Jennifer McBride noted no ongoing spill, but repairs are expected by January, though costs and the cause of the damage remain unknown. Resident Mike McCormack criticized the city’s deferred maintenance backlog, calling the incident a recurring issue. Nearby shop owner Terry Kraszewski expressed hope for a swift repair to restore the park. The park is expected to reopen in 2027.

item.title: Border Crossing Reopens After Screwworm Containment Measures
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: With tighter checks for flesh-eating screwworm, a border crossing reopens
Mexican cattle began moving through the Columbus, New Mexico border crossing on Monday after U.S. agriculture inspectors confirmed the area is free of the flesh-eating New World screwworm. The fly larva, which threatens the $113 billion U.S. cattle industry, had closed the port for nearly two years. Reopening the crossing, along with two others, aims to ease supply shortages as U.S. ranchers rebuild herds after droughts. Over 60 cases of screwworm have been confirmed in Texas and New Mexico, with the first U.S. wildlife case found in an elk. Officials say layers of testing, inspections, and insecticide dips ensure livestock are parasite-free. USDA undersecretary Dudley Hoskins emphasized continued monitoring, while New Mexico Border Authority executive Gerardo Fierro highlighted the $1 billion economic impact of the closure. A $610 million sterile fly production facility in Texas will aid eradication efforts. Cattle trade through Columbus and Santa Teresa accounts for a third of annual Mexican imports to the U.S. Another Arizona crossing is set to reopen in late November.

item.title: Four Corners Floods Kill One, Warnings Remain
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Flood warning lingers in Four Corners as soaked towns face sewage-tainted waters. 1 death reported
Floods in the Four Corners region caused by heavy rainfall led to one death in Santa Fe during a water rescue. A family attempting to cross a flooded arroyo lost a female passenger, who was found dead a mile away. The San Juan River reached 1.5 feet above flood stage, projected to crest at 31 feet, surpassing the 1927 record of 32 feet. Evacuations occurred in Utah and Colorado, with some residents returning early. Authorities warned of sewage and chemical contamination in floodwaters. In Farmington, New Mexico, hundreds remained evacuated and without power. Navajo Nation wastewater facilities were damaged, releasing sewage into the San Juan River. Officials urged caution as hazards like broken gas lines persisted. The Flatt family in Bloomfield evacuated after water surged 4 feet in 30 minutes, losing 22 chickens. Federal aid was requested as El Niño contributed to the heavy rainfall.

item.title: Pope Leo proceeds with South American tour after lung cancer surgery
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Pope's South American trip to go ahead as planned after lung cancer surgery
Pope Leo will proceed with his planned South American tour after undergoing lung cancer surgery. Diagnosed with a tumor on his right lung, he had successful surgery on 13 October in Rome. The 71-year-old will visit Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru from 6-17 November, following the original itinerary. He expressed enthusiasm for the trip, noting his connection to the continent. The Vatican confirmed his good health, citing tests showing localized cancer and a 90-minute surgery. His surgeon, Stefano Margaritora, stated there were no clinical reasons to cancel the trip. Pope Leo announced his diagnosis on 11 October during prayers, describing the nodule as 'well-contained' and early-stage. He canceled a planned October 27 Assisi trip per doctors' advice. The tour includes stops in Lima, Cuzco, and Chiclayo, where he lived years ago. Peru's Cardinal Castillo highlighted the Pope's engagement with young people, women in community kitchens, and indigenous communities. The Pope has Peruvian citizenship and a history of work in the U.S. and Peru.

item.title: Target adds new red to its color palette for store designs
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Target has added another red to its palette
Target introduced a new color, Cherry Stain, to balance its iconic red in store designs. The retailer's chief brand officer, Michelle Mesenburg, explained that the SoHo store's excessive use of red prompted the addition of the calmer hue. Cherry Stain, now part of Target's color palette, is used in the newly launched Beauty Studio department and some logos, combining with Pantone 186. The color was developed to complement the primary red and provide an alternative when the bullseye shade feels too intense. Mesenburg called the change a 'fresh chapter' for Target's branding, incorporating lessons from the SoHo remodel into broader store designs.

item.title: China Detains Panama-Flagged Ships Amid Canal Dispute
item.description:
Source: FP Foreign Policy Original headline: China Takes Its Lawfare to Sea
China has detained over 400 Panama-flagged ships at its ports between March and July 2026, escalating tensions over U.S. claims that Beijing controls the Panama Canal. The dispute originated from a 2025 U.S. presidential claim that China influenced the canal, leading to Panama’s Supreme Court overturning contracts for Hong Kong-owned port facilities. In response, China intensified inspections of Panama-flagged vessels, citing fishing boat collisions, though U.S. officials allege retaliatory measures. By April 2026, China accounted for 91% of detentions of Panama-flagged ships in the Asia-Pacific. Panama’s registry lost 500 ships—12.3% of its fleet—between late 2025 and August 2026, fearing penalties. China’s actions, framed as routine inspections, disrupted global shipping and cost Panama millions in licensing fees. The U.S. and allies condemned the detentions, with the Federal Maritime Commission accusing China of weaponizing port inspections. Panama’s government, which seized control of the ports after a court ruling, faces reputational risks as shipowners reflag vessels to avoid Chinese financing restrictions. The dispute highlights China’s use of maritime lawfare to retaliate against perceived threats to its interests, raising questions about global trade infrastructure as a tool for geopolitical pressure.

item.title: China Bypasses EU EV Tariffs Through Moroccan Supply Chain Expansion
item.description:
Source: FP Foreign Policy Original headline: China Is Building Its Way Around Europe’s EV Tariffs
China is circumventing European EV tariffs by establishing a supply chain in Morocco. Despite EU tariffs of up to 35% on Chinese EVs, Chinese firms are leveraging state-backed infrastructure and resource investments in Morocco to bypass restrictions. State-owned enterprises (SOEs) have developed key projects like the chemical processing unit in Khouribga, critical for EV battery production, while private companies such as BTR New Material Group and Gotion have established or planned factories in Tanger Tech City. China’s $10 billion investment in Morocco, concentrated in EV and energy sectors, enables localized production, reducing reliance on direct Chinese exports. Vehicles labeled as 'Made in Morocco' can enter Europe duty-free, avoiding both the 10% EU tariff and additional punitive charges on Chinese-made EVs. This strategy, supported by diplomatic shifts favoring Morocco’s Western Sahara claims, threatens the EU’s auto industry. Similar approaches are being tested in Thailand and the UAE, where Chinese SOEs and private firms benefit from tax incentives and strategic partnerships. The success of this model could reshape global EV markets by lowering costs and bypassing trade barriers.

item.title: Cybersecurity Experts Urge Focus on Trust Over Compliance
item.description:
Source: Harvard Business Review Original headline: To Build Effective Cyber Resilience, Invest in Trust
Organizations must prioritize building internal trust and relationships to enhance cyber resilience, experts argue. While compliance costs are easily tracked—covering training, policy enforcement, and awareness campaigns—measuring their impact on reducing breaches remains challenging. Verizon’s 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report found 62% of breaches involved human factors, a figure unchanged for three years. Despite rising compliance budgets, breach numbers have not declined, suggesting current approaches are insufficient. Cybersecurity leaders emphasize that fostering social capital—trust and shared understanding—within teams is critical for effective resilience. Quantifying compliance benefits remains elusive, prompting a shift toward relationship-building as a core strategy.

item.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan send envoys to Iran to avert war
item.description:
Source: Washington Post - World Original headline: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan send envoys to Iran in push to end war
Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan sent envoys to Tehran to meet Iranian leaders in a bid to prevent renewed military conflict. The meeting followed fears that the U.S. and Israel might resume strikes on Iran after Israel’s election on Tuesday and the U.S. midterms on November 3. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, facing a tight re-election race, has labeled Iran an 'existential threat' and ordered preparations for potential strikes. U.S. intelligence warned Iran was advancing plots against American officials. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian emphasized regional unity and cooperation, while a senior Iranian official expressed caution about the likelihood of de-escalation. The talks involved high-level officials including Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani Army Chief Asim Munir, and Turkish Intelligence Chief Ibrahim Kalin. Analysts warned that escalating tensions could lead to a war with no clear end, with Qatar and Gulf nations bracing for potential strikes. The visit followed Qatari mediation efforts and came amid growing regional anxiety over the possibility of renewed conflict.

item.title: Maryland schools serve invasive blue catfish to control population
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: Science Original headline: When an invasive fish is also tasty, Maryland schoolkids can help 'eat the problem'
Maryland schools are serving blue catfish cakes to students as part of an effort to combat the invasive species. Blue catfish, introduced in the 1970s, have become apex predators in the Chesapeake Bay, threatening native species and ecosystems. Beth Brewster, who oversees school food services, partnered with state officials to create a catfish cake recipe approved for USDA meals. The initiative, launched eight years ago, aims to reduce blue catfish populations by encouraging consumption. Schools in Maryland and Virginia now serve the dish, with students like Ben Rochon and Teagan Donovan enjoying the meal. Rocky Rice, a Maryland waterman, now fishes for blue catfish full-time, noting their mild flavor and year-round availability. However, processing challenges persist due to USDA inspection requirements, limiting processors to four in Maryland. Officials emphasize that eradication is impossible, so eating the fish is the best solution. 'Eat the problem and save the bay,' says Jenn Lovewell of Bay2Tray, which connects schools and restaurants to invasive fish markets.

item.title: Dictionary.com names 'maxxing' 2026 Word of the Year
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: 'Maxxing' selected as Dictionary.com word of the year
Dictionary.com named 'maxxing' as its 2026 Word of the Year, reflecting a cultural focus on optimization. The term, short for maximizing, is used to describe pushing activities to their fullest extent. Steve Johnson, director of lexicography, noted its rise mirrors a society obsessed with extracting maximum value. Digital media usage of 'maxxing' surged 19 times in August 2026 compared to 2025. Social media users, particularly Gen Z, employ it in phrases like 'proteinmaxxing' and 'sleepmaxxing,' with influencer Clavicular gaining followers for 'looksmaxxing.' Johnson highlighted the term's expanding uses, from embracing it to subverting it for humor. The word's roots trace back to 1990s pop culture, like Will Smith's 'maxin' in The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air. Teachers like Lauren Cella and linguist Vanessa Croft observed its rapid evolution, noting Gen Z now uses it ironically while older generations adopt it differently. The term's fleeting nature underscores how digital media accelerates linguistic change.

item.title: Passenger's Alleged Hijack Threat Forces Flight Diversion
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: ‘Crash ur row only’: United flight turned around after passenger allegedly said he’d ‘hijack’ plane
A United Airlines flight was diverted back to Las Vegas after a passenger allegedly sent a message midair threatening to 'hijack' the plane. The 25-year-old man, whose message included 'crash ur row only,' was arrested on charges of making terroristic threats and providing false information about an act of terrorism. Las Vegas police detained him after a report of the threat on a Saturday night flight bound for Newark, New Jersey. The flight, carrying 150 passengers, returned to the airport less than an hour after takeoff. United confirmed the diversion to address a 'potential security concern,' with the flight delayed overnight and departing Newark on Sunday. The Federal Aviation Administration announced an investigation into the incident, noting over 1,400 unruly passenger incidents in 2026. The man's initial court appearance is scheduled for Tuesday, though his attorney did not immediately respond to comment requests.

item.title: AI Startup Simile Raises $300M to Build Digital Consumer Models
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: This AI startup raised $300 million to build digital versions of consumers
Simile, an AI startup co-founded by Joon Sung Park, raised $300 million at a $2 billion valuation to develop digital clones of consumers. Park described the technology as creating 'a foundation model of human behavior' that simulates how people might act in various scenarios. Businesses can use the platform to test products, marketing campaigns, and store layouts by defining target audiences and asking questions through a web interface. Simile partners with retailers like CVS, Walmart, and financial institutions, using data from 40 million global participants and behavioral metrics like transaction and mobility data. Park called the ability to simulate people and answer any questions 'a superpower for these companies,' as it allows real-time insights without relying on traditional surveys. The startup's tools aim to enhance personalization and decision-making for industries ranging from retail to entertainment.

item.title: Nike CEO Schedules Family Time as Nonnegotiable Priority
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Nike CEO Elliott Hill knew he’d always miss breakfast with his kids. He made another part of the day nonnegotiable.
Nike CEO Elliott Hill schedules family time as nonnegotiable priorities. Hill, who returned as CEO in 2024 after retiring in 2020, follows a structured routine with set sleep and wake times, daily workouts, and calendar-based commitments. He lists personal priorities—family, friends, growth, and work—then builds specific obligations into his schedule. For example, he ensures dinner with his children by blocking time to leave the office, despite missing breakfast. He also schedules parent-teacher conferences and shifts work trips to avoid conflicts. Hill emphasized writing priorities on paper and integrating them into calendars to maintain balance. Other executives, like Leah Solivan and Becca Millstein, share similar organizational habits, though Hill’s focus on family time stands out. His approach reflects a deliberate strategy to balance professional and personal life through planning.

item.title: Father Killed While Assisting Daughter on I-15 in San Diego
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Father killed while helping daughter stranded on I-15 in San Diego
A man was killed early Monday after being struck by a vehicle while assisting his daughter, who was stranded on northbound Interstate 15 in San Diego. The daughter, driving a Mazda, had stopped in the center divider due to a possible flat tire and called her father for help. CHP reported the father was side-swiped by a Toyota Corolla, killing him. The collision triggered a second crash when an SUV struck the Corolla. Both drivers were hospitalized, though their conditions were unclear. A fifth vehicle sideswiped one of the vehicles involved, with the driver unharmed. The daughter and her children were not injured. CHP closed northbound I-15 near Clairemont Mesa Boulevard, diverting traffic to State Route 52 and recommending alternate routes. Traffic backed up to Aero Drive as crews responded to the scene. The initial call for the collision came in around 3:30 a.m.

item.title: National Weather Service warns of record high tides threatening San Diego beaches
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Pronostican mareas altas extremas que podrían dañar las playas del condado de San Diego
National Weather Service warns of record high tides up to 8 feet along San Diego County coast from Sunday to Thursday, risking erosion and flooding. Chandler Price, meteorologist, notes previous records of 7 feet 8 inches in 2015 could be surpassed. Low-lying areas like Imperial Beach, Cardiff Reef, and Tamarack State Park face impacts. A coastal flood warning remains until 1 p.m. Thursday. Price cites Earth’s closest approach to the Sun and El Niño’s ocean warming as causes. Scripps Pier surface temperatures hit 73°F, 8 degrees above average. Tamarack Beach has suffered severe erosion from high tides and storms, with waves reaching 3-4 feet. Metrolink canceled rail service between Orange County and San Diego due to tides.

item.title: San Diego Man Rescued From Apartment Roof After Tree Trimming Attempt
item.description:
Source: NBC 7 San Diego Original headline: San Diego man rescued from apartment building roof after attempting to tree trim
A 72-year-old man was rescued from the roof of a three-story apartment building in San Diego's Colina Del Sol neighborhood after attempting to trim tree branches. Firefighters arrived around 1 p.m. Sunday and used a pulley system to lower him to the ground in a basket within 50 minutes. He was evaluated and released by medics on scene. The San Diego Fire-Rescue Department deployed two fire engines, one fire truck, an urban search and rescue unit, an ambulance, a battalion chief, and a shift commander. Authorities emphasized the importance of preparing for potential El Nino storms but urged residents to do so safely. Spokesperson Jose Ysea noted the man had used a ladder to access the roof but was unable to descend on his own.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: TikTok Shop Entrepreneur Earns Six Figures with Less Than $500
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: How a 6-figure TikTok Shop entrepreneur got started with less than $500
Talon Krebs, a 23-year-old TikTok Shop affiliate, earned six figures last year through his full-time role promoting products via the app. He told Business Insider that TikTok Shop is one of the most profitable business models he's encountered. Krebs started with less than $500, using a phone, existing products, and a personal account with 24,000 followers. To join TikTok Shop, affiliates must meet follower thresholds: 1,000 for the pilot program or 5,000 for the main program. Krebs recommended repurposing items he already owned to minimize costs, and he paid a $1,500 community fee in installments. His strategy includes creating engaging hooks within 30-50 second videos, addressing viewer pain points, and using direct product tags to drive sales. He emphasized that success hinges on understanding what stops users from scrolling and structuring videos with a clear hook, explanation, and call to action.

item.title: Encinitas City Council to Debate Rent Moratorium Options
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Encinitas to debate proposed mobile home park rent moratorium
Encinitas City Council will debate two rent moratorium proposals for mobile home parks. Both options allow rent increases of 4% or 75% of the San Diego CPI (4.7% annually), whichever is lower. Park owners may petition for higher increases, triggering a public hearing. The proposed measures are less than a previously rescinded 20% hike from Riviera Mobile Home Park. Residents argue they are trapped, owning homes but renting land from corporations. The city has 11 parks with 729 spaces. Council members noted only one park had a significant rate increase, which was dropped. An urgency ordinance would take effect immediately with a supermajority vote, while a non-urgency version requires regular legislative process. The meeting starts at 6 p.m. at City Hall.

item.title: San Diego Pride Executive Director Resigns Amid Financial Challenges
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: San Diego Pride executive director resigns amid 'financial challenges'
San Diego Pride's Executive Director, KishaLynn Elliott, will resign starting November as the organization faces financial challenges. The organization cited 'significant financial challenges that require difficult decisions about our organizational structure and operations' in a statement. Elliott's resignation comes amid efforts to stabilize the group, with the board planning to determine a new leadership structure and 'sustainable path forward.' The organization expressed gratitude for Elliott's leadership during the challenging period. A Community Listening Session is scheduled for Tuesday, Oct. 27, from 6:30 p.m. at St. Paul's Cathedral in San Diego to discuss the organization's future.

item.title: 6-Year-Old Boy Found After Amber Alert Issued
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: 6-year-old boy at center of Amber Alert located, CHP says
California Highway Patrol deactivated an Amber Alert after locating a 6-year-old boy believed to have been taken by his grandfather. Joseph Garcia was last seen near Collins Avenue and Lemon Street in Orange County around 4 p.m. Officials say he may be with Frank Ramirez, 47, who is driving a blue 1995 GMC Sonoma with license plates 5B30127. Garcia is described as 3’ 7”, 65 pounds, with brown hair and brown eyes, last seen in a beige shirt, blue shorts, and black shoes. Ramirez is 5’ 6”, 180 pounds, with black hair and hazel eyes, last seen in a gray tank top and shorts. The Amber Alert covered Riverside, San Diego, Los Angeles, and Orange counties. Authorities urged anyone with information to call 911.

item.title: AI Enhances Scams Targeting Older Americans; Experts Warn of New Red Flags
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: AI is making scams against older Americans more convincing. Experts share how to spot the new red flags.
AI-powered scams targeting older Americans are becoming more convincing, with experts warning of new red flags. Cybersecurity researchers discovered critical flaws in PHP, a language used by 70% of websites, prompting emergency patches. These vulnerabilities could enable attackers to hijack servers and execute remote code. Experts emphasize that AI enhances scam sophistication, including deepfakes, voice cloning, and targeted phishing. AARP reports 4 in 10 older Americans have lost money to fraud, with romance scams and impersonation scams being prevalent. Craig Newmark advises basic cyber hygiene, like multi-factor authentication and pausing before clicking links. Don Grant highlights AI-assisted romance scams, such as a case where a 60-something man lost $1,200 to a fake girlfriend. Alex Jacquez notes AI enables large-scale, sophisticated fraud, with Interpol stating AI-enhanced fraud is 4.5 times more profitable than traditional methods. Amy Nofziger stresses the need for systemic fixes, including better data protection by companies. Ali Tager warns against giveaway and phishing scams, urging vigilance with crypto and private keys. Experts urge families to educate loved ones, use free resources like AARP’s Fraud Watch Network, and remain cautious without panic.

item.title: Jordan Strikes Syria After Church Attack Tied to Terrorists
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Jordan says its military struck 'militant hideouts' in Syria after deadly church attack
Jordan's air force struck suspected militant hideouts in southern Syria after linking the deadly attack on a Greek Orthodox church to terrorist groups. The strikes, coordinated with Damascus, reportedly killed at least five civilians, including women and children, according to Syrian officials. Jordanian security forces arrested three men in Karak province following a dawn shootout, wounding all suspects but suffering no casualties. Interior Minister Mazen Al-Faraya stated the suspects, identified early in the investigation, were subdued after fierce resistance. King Abdullah II ordered an 'iron fist' response against those undermining Jordanian unity. Relatives of victims expressed relief over the arrests, though no group has claimed responsibility for the attack. Attacks on Christian minorities are rare in Jordan, a stable state with U.S. and Israeli ties.

item.title: San Diego coastal flood warning triggers flooding in Mission Beach
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Coastal flood warning hits San Diego as high tides send bay water into Mission Beach yards
A coastal flood warning is in effect for San Diego's coastline due to high tides causing flooding. In Mission Beach, residents face recurring issues as a sand berm failed to prevent water from entering properties. Steve Nipper, a long-time resident, reported water reaching his front door around 8:30 a.m. on Sunday, despite the berm's intended purpose. Nipper, who has lived there for 30 years, described the flooding as regular but noted this instance was particularly severe. The National Weather Service warned of potential flooding up to 1.7 feet above normal tide levels through Thursday afternoon. Nipper, who owns a dog rescue, expressed concerns about cleaning his yard to protect the animals and is using sandbags and a sealed fence to mitigate further damage. He hopes the city will build a larger berm but remains optimistic despite the challenges.

item.title: U.S. urges Venezuela to allow Machado's return
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: US told Venezuelan authorities that opposition leader Machado should be allowed to return
Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated the Trump administration urged Venezuela's interim authorities to allow opposition leader María Corina Machado to return weeks ago. Machado, who had been in hiding since 2025, returned to Venezuela over the weekend after being in Norway since December 2025. Rubio said the U.S. emphasized Machado's right to return as a Venezuelan citizen, noting only temporary concerns after June earthquakes. The administration also pushed for electoral reforms to enable free elections by 2027, with interim President Delcy Rodríguez agreeing to a reform blueprint. Rubio warned the U.S. would monitor progress, stressing the need for economic stability, institutional rebuilding, and press freedom. Machado, who gave her Nobel Peace Prize to Trump, returned as Rodríguez, Maduro's former vice president, faces extended tenure without scheduled elections.
